demo.detailsBody: Renlio reads CSV, TSV and Excel exports from most banks and cards, detecting the date, description, amount and balance columns on its own. It understands both dd/mm/yyyy and mm/dd/yyyy dates, and both 260.000 and 15.99 number formats. A charge only counts as a subscription when it repeats at least twice on a regular cycle with amounts within 35% of each other.

sources.title: Four ways to get subscriptions into Renlio
sources.lead: No single source sees everything. Renlio combines all four — and whatever is still missing, you add by hand.

items.title: Add by hand
items.bestFor: Plans that never touch a card
items.body: A gym paid in cash, a plan split with friends, a service billed through an e-wallet. Type the name, amount, cycle and next renewal date — about 30 seconds. This is also how you add anything Renlio did not find.

items.title: Import a statement
items.body: Upload a CSV, Excel or PDF bank and card statement. Renlio looks for charges that repeat on a cycle, so it catches plans that never send a confirmation email. You can try it in the section above.

items.title: Watch Gmail
items.body: Connect Gmail or Outlook once and Renlio picks up new receipts and updates renewal dates on its own. Renlio requests read access to find receipt emails; it cannot send or delete anything.

items.title: Forward receipts
items.body: Renlio gives you your own address. Forward a receipt there and you are done — Renlio only ever sees the emails you deliberately send, nothing else in your inbox.

features.title: What Renlio does with that data

items.title: You confirm, not the AI
items.body: Every plan detected from a statement or an email goes through a review screen with a confidence score. You keep, edit or drop each line before Renlio saves anything.

items.title: Total-cost dashboard
items.body: Monthly and yearly subscription totals, all four sources merged into one list, sortable by amount or by next renewal date.

items.title: Warned before the charge
items.body: An email a few days before a plan is billed, so you can still decide to keep or cancel — instead of finding out after the money is gone.

security.title: Renlio does not ask for access it does not use
security.lead: An app that reads bank statements has to prove it is safe, not just say so. Here is what Renlio does and does not do.

items.title: No bank login
items.body: Renlio never asks for your internet banking password or an OTP code. You hand it a statement file you exported yourself.

items.title: Analysis on your device
items.body: The demo on this page reads and analyses your statement entirely in JavaScript, in your browser. No network request carries the file contents.

items.title: No card numbers stored
items.body: Renlio only needs the date, description and amount of a transaction. Card and account numbers are not stored anywhere.

items.title: Delete everything in one click
items.body: You can remove all of your data from Renlio at any time, without emailing a request or waiting for approval.

items.title: Minimal Gmail access
items.body: Renlio only requests read access to find receipt emails; it cannot send or delete messages. You can revoke access at any time in your Google account security settings — or skip it entirely and forward receipts instead.

items.title: Your data is not for sale
items.body: Renlio does not sell, share or trade your spending data with any third party.

pricing.title: Free. No card needed.
pricing.note: No limit on plans, no limit on imports.

faq.title: What people ask before trusting Renlio

items.q: Does Renlio need my internet banking password?
items.a: No. Renlio never asks for a password, an OTP code or any banking credential. You upload a statement file exported from your banking app, or paste a few transaction lines into the page.

items.q: Is my statement uploaded to a server?
items.a: The analysis on this page runs entirely in your browser: the file is read by JavaScript on your own machine, and no network request carries its contents. You can verify this in the Network tab of DevTools.

items.q: What about plans I pay in cash or through an e-wallet?
items.a: You add those by hand. Type the service name, amount, cycle and next renewal date, and Renlio counts it in your total and reminds you like any other plan. A card statement cannot see cash, so adding by hand is how your list becomes genuinely complete.

items.q: If I connect Gmail, what can Renlio see?
items.a: Renlio requests read access to find receipt emails and cannot send or delete messages; you can revoke it at any time in your Google account security settings. If you would rather not grant inbox access, use forwarding instead: Renlio gives you your own address and only ever sees the emails you deliberately send there.

items.q: Which banks and file formats does Renlio support?
items.a: Renlio reads CSV, TSV and Excel exports from most banks and credit cards, detecting the date, description, amount and balance columns automatically. The demo on this page accepts CSV and pasted text, including Vietnamese statements that use dots as thousands separators and dd/mm/yyyy dates.

items.q: What if Renlio gets it wrong?
items.a: Every subscription Renlio finds has to pass through your review before it is saved. Each one carries a confidence score based on how many times it repeated, how regular the cycle is, and how stable the amount is — so you know which ones to double-check. Renlio does not trust the machine blindly.

items.q: Does Renlio cancel subscriptions for me?
items.a: No. Renlio detects, totals and reminds; cancelling is something you do on the provider's own site. Renlio has no access to your accounts at those services.
Yes. Subscription detection, the total-cost dashboard and payment reminders are all free, with no credit card required.

privacyBody: Renlio processes statement data to detect recurring charges. The analysis on the home page runs entirely in your browser: file contents are never sent to a Renlio server.
When you sign up for payment reminders, Renlio stores your email address for exactly that purpose. You can request deletion at any time by writing to hello@renlio.site.
Renlio does not sell, share or trade your spending data with any third party. Renlio does not store card numbers, account numbers or banking credentials.

This site uses Google Analytics to count visits and see where readers come from. It sets a cookie in your browser and sends traffic data to Google. It cannot read the statement you paste into the Try it section, because that runs entirely in your browser and is never sent anywhere. You can block Google Analytics with an ad blocker.
termsBody: Renlio is a tool that helps you track subscription costs. Detection results are produced algorithmically and need your own review before you rely on them for financial decisions.
Renlio is not a financial institution, does not give investment advice and does not make transactions on your behalf. Cancelling a service is something you do on the provider's own site.
You are responsible for the data you upload and confirm that you only use statements you are entitled to.
The service is provided as is. Renlio works to be accurate but does not guarantee that every one of your subscriptions will be detected.
